checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: Checklist item arms_running reports '5 running: tp-7pct, hold-12h, entry-8pct, sl-5pct, vol-4x' and every arm in the arena is labelled [running/confirm].
findings.problem: entry-8pct has live_n=3 and vol-4x has live_n=7 against a planned confirm n=600, and 18 trades are still open across the fleet. Calling these arms 'running in confirm' is metadata asserting a state the trade counts do not establish — the same META failure that hid firstred-1h for six weeks, inverted. The check should report live_n per arm, not just registry status.

findings.claim: Arms are reported with screen_dWR values — sl-5pct screen_dWR=5.29pp, hold-12h screen_dWR=3.23pp, tp-7pct screen_dWR=-3.42pp — as the headline discriminator between arms.
findings.problem: Those deltas come from the screen tier, which is backfill (events by tier: backfill=4764, live=49). The checklist itself states backfill_cannot_promote and that only live-tape evidence can promote, yet the screen deltas are the only effect sizes carried into the arena display, and no live dWR is reported alongside them. A reader ranks arms on evidence the loop has already declared non-promoting.

findings.claim: entry-8pct is scored as an arm on the shared detection stream, alongside control and placebo which show screen_n=1550.
findings.problem: entry-8pct has screen_n=496 and vol-4x screen_n=866 versus 1550 for control — these arms are scored on a strict subset of the shared events, because pump_pct=8.0 and vol_threshold=4.0 remove detections. The paired_population check reports '4813 events in the shared window; every arm has seen all of them', which is true of exposure but not of scoring. Comparing screen_wr=51.613 (n=496) to control screen_wr=49.935 (n=1550) is an unpaired comparison presented as paired.

findings.claim: paired_population is green: 'Every arm scored on identical events'.
findings.problem: The detail line establishes that all arms saw the 4813 events and that open trades are excluded, but the differing screen_n values (1550 / 866 / 496) show the scored sets are not identical. The check is green for a reason — shared exposure — that does not establish the property it claims, which is shared scoring.

findings.claim: declined counts are reported per arm (control/placebo/tp-7pct/hold-12h/sl-5pct declined=33, vol-4x declined=40, entry-8pct declined=46).
findings.problem: control and placebo are supposed to be behaviourally identical — placebo_inert confirms b=0 c=0 discordant pairs — yet both show declined=33, which means the control arm itself is declining a third of live-eligible detections for reasons the context never states. No mechanism or rule for declines is given anywhere, so a large, unexplained live-sample filter sits upstream of every live_n in the arena.

findings.claim: entry_granularity_declared is non-critical, with the note that 'arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel'.
findings.problem: That shared-kernel argument fails precisely for the arms whose parameter is the pump threshold. The kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups), so entry-8pct's boundary sits at a different effective live threshold than the kernel's 8.0 — the bias is not common-mode for an entry_trigger arm. Marking this non-critical understates the exposure for the one arm the measurement bias directly moves.
